title: FairShare: tenant burst fairness vs latency/cost (draft)
content:
Executive summary:
This draft records an exploratory benchmark suite focused on tenant-level fairness during transient bursts and how fairness policies interact with latency percentiles and unit cost. We tested three serving policies (fairshare-strict, best-effort, slot-priority) across three model variants and on two topology classes (edge, core). Results show: 
- Fairshare-strict improves max-min fairness at the expense of ~10–25% p99 latency inflation for bursty tenants compared to best-effort.
- Slot-priority keeps p99 low for high-paying tenants but drives fairness index down and increases aggregate cost by ~8% due to inefficient slot utilization.
- Quantized variant reduces $/M tokens by ~18% and partially absorbs p99 penalty under fairshare (less degradation than base model).

Goals and context:
- Product question: is a tenant-facing "fairshare" option justified for mid-market accounts that expect predictable throughput during bursts without needing dedicated capacity?
- Tradeoffs: fairness (ratio of delivered throughput across tenants during bursts) vs tail-latency (p99) and per-token cost.
- Audience: product managers (Optimize), platform SRE, runtime owners, and solutions engineering for customer-facing docs.

Workloads and patterns:
- Baseline steady: 500 qps constant, 20k sessions, short-turn chat (avg 30 tokens).
- Burst-sawtooth: 30m sustained with periodic 60s bursts (x6 qps) on a subset of tenants.
- Microburst: 10–20s spikes (x20–x40) arriving from 10% tenants (simulating conversational assistants).
- Long-session: fewer sessions, longer prompt (avg 300 tokens) to stress KV cache behavior.

Model variants:
- base-v1 (FP16 unfused kernels)
- quant-v1 (8-bit quantized weights, CPU/GPU mixed kernels)
- distill-v1 (smaller layer count, lower compute)

Topology:
- edge (g4x-like core but colocated near region; lower NVLink bandwidth, higher cold-starts)
- core (high-throughput instance with NVLink, better packing)

Serving policies tested:
- fairshare-strict: enforces proportional throughput per tenant during contention; preemption allowed at request boundary.
- best-effort: first-come-first-serve with opportunistic batching.
- slot-priority: reserved slots for high-tier tenants; remaining capacity pooled.

Metrics collected (per tenant and system-wide):
- p50, p90, p99 latencies (ms)
- throughput observed (qps) per tenant group
- fairness index = min_throughput / max_throughput (during the burst window)
- $/1M tokens (estimated from amortized GPU time + infra cost)
- slot utilization % and cache hit rate (where applicable)

Key experiment matrix (representative subset):
- 3 models x 2 topologies x 3 policies x 4 workloads = 72 runs (each run 45–90m)

Representative results (selected slices):
Table: microburst, edge topology, burst window summary

+----------------+-----------+---------+---------+---------+-----------+
| Tenant Group   | Policy    | p50(ms) | p90(ms) | p99(ms) | $/1M toks |
+----------------+-----------+---------+---------+---------+-----------+
| High-duty      | best-effort| 42     | 110     | 520     | 240       |
| High-duty      | fairshare | 45      | 130     | 640     | 250       |
| High-duty      | slot-pri  | 38      | 95      | 310     | 275       |
| Low-duty       | best-effort| 48     | 220     | 2100    | 240       |
| Low-duty       | fairshare | 50      | 175     | 720     | 255       |
| Low-duty       | slot-pri  | 95      | 450     | 1800    | 260       |
+----------------+-----------+---------+---------+---------+-----------+

Notes:
- best-effort shows extreme p99 inflation for small tenants during microbursts (p99 > 2s), indicating starvation.
- fairshare brings low-duty p99 down dramatically (2100 -> 720) but increases high-duty p99 by ~23% (520 -> 640).
- slot-pri protects high-duty p99 but increases cost (slots underutilized during non-bursty periods).

Fairness index (same slice):
- best-effort: 0.12 (very poor)
- fairshare: 0.68 (good)
- slot-pri: 0.21 (poor for low-duty)

Cost breakdown insight:
- Cost modeled as amortized GPU seconds + storage (KV cache) + infra premium for slot reservations. For edge nodes, preemption and packing inefficiencies increase per-token cost.
- Quantized model: $/1M tokens reduced by ~18% on average; p99 increases slightly overall but shows better resilience under fairshare because lower per-request runtime frees slots faster.

ASCII sparklines (p99 over time during a 10m burst window)
- best-effort (low-duty): |____/~~~~~~/~~~~~~~~~|  (ramp to long tail)
- fairshare (low-duty):   |___/~~~__/~~~~_|  (contained tail)
- slot-pri (low-duty):    |____/~~~~~~~~~~|  (long tail when preempted)

Operational observations:
- Preemption semantics matter: request-boundary preemption causes latency spikes for long-decoding requests. For long-session workload, fairshare had unexpected p99 spikes due to preemption waste; we should test heartbeat-based cooperative checkpoints in decode loop.
- KV cache: cache hit-rate dropped 6–9% under strict fairshare (due to more tenant mixing), which raised tokens consumed per inference for long-session workloads.
- Billing signaling: slot-priority requires clearer UX about expected cost premiums; customers misinterpret "priority" as only latency benefit when it also changes $/token economics.

Recommendations (short-term):
1) Ship a "fairshare-beta" toggle targeted at mid-market tenants: default = off, opt-in with guidance.
2) Offer hybrid policy: fairshare for a short grace window (30–120s) then degrade to best-effort — this reduces p99 penalty for heavy tenants while protecting small ones in brief spikes.
3) Prioritize quantization for fairshare use-case; quant-v1 shows best combined reduction in $/token and mitigated p99 impact.
4) Add a decode-level cooperative checkpoint RFC to reduce preemption waste for long-session workloads.

Next steps / experiments to run:
- Repeat core topology runs with increased packing (higher duty factor) to measure slot-pri amortization thresholds.
- Add more granular fairness metric (Jain's index) and per-tenant SLA curves to quantify tradeoffs for sales conversations.
- Prototype the hybrid short-grace fairshare policy (30s smoothing) and measure p99 delta vs fairness index.

Appendix: quick-run notes and reproducibility
- Bench harness: github.com/redwood-inference/bench/fairshare-2029 (see linked PR).
- Driver flags: --workload=microburst --policy=fairshare-strict --model=quant-v1 --topology=edge --burst-mult=20 --seed=73
- Typical single-run artifacts: latency histograms (ndjson), billing estimator traces (.csv), slot-utilization trace (.jsonl). Stored in S3: s3://redwood-bench/fairshare/2029-07-12/{run-id}/

Open questions / discussion points for PM and runtime owners:
- Is fairness an upsell feature (marketable) or should it be a platform default at lower tiers?
- How to present cost vs fairness in Console: explicit tradeoff slider, or pre-baked policies?
- Is the slot-priority premium defensible given the observed ~8–12% aggregate cost uplift?

Draft status notes:
- This is an internal draft intended to seed discussion. Data artifacts available in S3; I can produce slide-ready charts if product wants to push to customers.

Author: Priya Menon (product-optimize)
Reviewed-by: Liam O'Connor, Xiao Li (engineering)
